messages:
Talia Benson: Kicking off the “Perf baseline & representative workload suite (Q1 2026)” work. Parent Linear is up: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/perf-baseline-representative-workload-suite-q1-2026

Talia Benson: Logistics: can we do a 45m kickoff this week? I’m holding Thu 10:00–10:45 PT (needs Runtime + SRE + Evals + Release Eng). Agenda: scope/non-goals, initial model list, traffic-shape shortlist, owners, and next-step milestones.

Mateo Alvarez: :thumbsup: works for me. Let’s make sure we leave with clear DRI for workload suite + harness + variance budget.

Noah Patel: Thu 10 PT ok. Can you drop the doc we’ll use as scratchpad?

Talia Benson: Yep — Drive kickoff notes doc (messy, WIP): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1yQ1-2026-perf-baselines (see “perf-baseline-kickoff-notes-2026-01-06”).

Marcus Reed: I can own “workload suite repo + baseline artifact packaging” (ENG-4823-ish). Also can bring what we have from benchmark-lab runner.

Rina Kobayashi: I’m in for harness/runner ownership. We should align on output schema + env pinning (driver/CUDA/runtime build metadata). I’ll come with a proposal.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel team can cover microbench + kernel sweep tie-ins, but for baseline suite, we need to pick models that actually stress prefill + decode paths. Grace can help define the “must include” shapes.

Grace Kim: +1. For kernels we care about (a) long context prefill, (b) small batch decode under streaming, (c) mixed prompt length batching pressure.

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduling team here. Please include a “bursty concurrency + mixed tenants” shape — that’s where tail latency explodes. Also need agreed TTFT/TPOT definitions (streaming vs non-streaming).

Sean Gallagher: SRE perspective: please don’t make this depend on production-only signals. We need fully reproducible + sanitized/aggregated shapes. Also we need an explicit variance budget so we can gate without paging for noise.

Jonas Weber: Evals/Perf can help with methodology + run counts (stat treatment). We should agree: TTFT, TPOT, e2e latency, throughput, error rate; report p50/p95/p99; warm vs cold cache.

Claire Dubois: I can drive the representative traffic-shape taxonomy (ENG-4822). For kickoff, I’ll bring a first draft of shapes + rationale mapped to customer patterns.

Talia Benson: Great. Initial owner mapping draft:
- Traffic-shape taxonomy + workload list: @Claire Dubois (w/ Jonas + Sofia input)
- Harness/runner + schema: @Rina Kobayashi
- Suite maintenance + artifact/versioning: @Marcus Reed
- Kernel microbench tie-ins: @Hiro Tanaka / @Grace Kim
- Variance budget + gating requirements: @Sean Gallagher + @Jonas Weber

Vanessa Ortiz: FYI fleet variance is going to be a problem if we don’t lock SKU + driver. For kickoff can we decide “golden” hardware/regions for baselines? (at least 1–2 SKUs to start)

Sahana Iyer: Release Eng/CI side: I’ll join kickoff. We should plan staged rollout (warn-only → soft fail → hard fail) for perf gates. Also need to define what runs on PR vs nightly.

Noah Patel: Re: initial model shortlist — proposing we baseline top-served chat + long context + small model:
- Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (primary)
- Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (alt, different arch behavior)
- Mixtral-8x22B-Instruct (MoE)
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (latency floor / edge)
Maybe add one long-context tuned variant if we have it in catalog.

Hiro Tanaka: Looks good. Mixtral is important for kernel selection stability. Also: pick a quantized profile we actually ship (e.g., int8/FP8) so the baseline matches reality.

Sofia Ivanova: Traffic shapes I’d like in v0:
1) Streaming chat “interactive”: prompt ~200–800 tok, output ~100–300 tok, conc 1–16
2) Long-context RAG: prompt 8k–32k tok, output 200–800 tok, conc 1–4
3) Summarization/non-streaming: prompt 2k–8k, output 1k–4k, conc 1–8
4) Bursty concurrency ramp: 0→N over 30–60s, mixed prompt lengths
5) Cache scenarios: cold, warm (50% hit), hot (90% hit)

Claire Dubois: +1. I’ll translate those into canonical “shapes” with distributions (not fixed lengths) and define how we generate them synthetically.

Sean Gallagher: Please explicitly include “mixed tenants” (two traffic classes sharing the same pool) so we can see fairness + queueing effects. That’s where p99 surprises happen.

Rina Kobayashi: For runner: I’ll propose we stamp every result with (git SHA, model version, runtime build id, driver/CUDA, kernel-autotune seed, region, instance type). Otherwise we can’t reproduce.

Talia Benson: Awesome. Kickoff calendar invite going out now with links:
- Linear parent: ENG-4821 https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/perf-baseline-representative-workload-suite-q1-2026
- Drive notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1yQ1-2026-perf-baselines
Please add any “must decide” items in the Drive doc before Thu.

Mateo Alvarez: One more must-decide: what we’re comfortable publishing (even internally) vs restricted. We can keep that separate, but baseline suite must avoid sensitive prompts.

Jonas Weber: I’ll add a section in the notes: methodology defaults (trials, warmup, CI) + what confidence interval we need for gating.

Talia Benson: :thumbsup: thanks all. See you Thu.
